label: Late in the episode, z dips at D1 after a1 reaching S2, and when belief favours S1.
short_terms: (phase == D1) * ((prev_state - prev_action)==1) * ep_trial ;; belief_lo * ep_trial * ep_trial
terms: (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 u") * ep_trial ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 r") * ep_trial ;; belief_lo * ep_trial ;; (phase==D1)*last_is("a1 S1 u")*ep_trial ;; ((tv("action",-1)==1)+(tv("action",-2)==1)+(tv("action",-3)==1))*ep_trial ;; (phase==D1)*(prev_action==2)*ep_trial ;; (prev_action==1)*ep_trial
explanation: Update gate unit 44 sits near 1 (mean 0.993) and drops over the episode; the timing baseline already captures that late decline. Beyond timing, the dips grow with episode trial: at D1 they are largest after an a1 choice that reached S2 by a rare transition, whether rewarded or not (about -0.02 on average, as low as 0.8 near trial 99). On every phase the gate is also lower the more the ideal observer believes S1 is good (graded belief_lo), with the opposite sign when S2 is believed good. That matches the a1-lowers / a2-raises pattern in the choice tables. All terms are scaled by ep_trial because the deviations are concentrated late in the episode. The free fit (a1 run length, other D1 previous-trial patterns) adds almost nothing (test 0.449 vs short 0.435). This beats the additive all-cue ceiling (0.38) because of the episode-time interaction. Some of the large late D1 dips after unrewarded a1-S1 trials stay underpredicted. Uses observed variables only.

issues: The claims hold up. Recorded short form scores test R^2 beyond timing 0.435. Each part matters: the belief term alone gives 0.214 and the two D1 a1->S2 terms alone give 0.284. Both weights are negative, so z is lower after a1->S2 at D1 and lower as belief_lo rises toward S1, as the label says. The residual table agrees: at D1, a1 S2 r is -0.022 and a1 S2 u is -0.017, while every other previous-trial pattern is within +-0.006.

The rewarded and unrewarded a1->S2 terms have similar weights (-0.00045 and -0.00029 per trial), so they say one thing: a1 reached S2 by a rare transition. One term, (prev_state - prev_action)==1, works as well (0.426 with a linear belief term).

The graded log-odds matter. Swapping belief_lo for raw belief, prev_action, or an a1 count over the last 3 trials drops the score to 0.37 or lower. The belief effect is not just a stand-in for the last choice.

Linear ep_trial is a poor fit to the late-episode shape. The timing decline is concentrated in the last decile, and belief_lo*ep_trial*ep_trial does better (0.450 with the merged a1->S2 term, 0.459 with the original two last_is terms).

Misses show no large systematic class. Mean errors by phase are about 0.001 and errors by phase x previous trial are all 0.005 or less. The worst windows are trials 93-99 with long a1 runs, where actual z (about 0.80-0.88 at D1) is well below predicted (about 0.93). That is the largest-magnitude tail, not one pattern class. Adding a D1 no-reward term barely helps (0.462) and gets a positive weight, so these deep dips stay unexplained.
The free fit adds little over the short form (0.449 vs 0.435), which supports the short form as the interpretation.
